newsitem.title: USA: Raymond James mulls sale of muni CPI-floater bonds.
newsitem.headline: Raymond James mulls sale of muni CPI-floater bonds.

text.p: Raymond James & Associates said Wednesday it is working on a sale of from $100 million to $150 million of bonds for a Florida issuer that would be indexed to the Consumer Price Index.
"It's in the works," said Peter Delahunt, national sales manager for the firm's municipal bond department. "The banker hopes to finalize details with the issuer in the near future," he added.
Goldman Sachs recently launched the first sale of inflation-indexed municipal bonds with a $40 million sale of tax-exempt bonds for City of Orlando, Fla.

The Raymond James official said that its deal likley would be similar to the Goldman offering, and taxable debt sold by governmental entities and corporations, as the principal would be set, but the coupon would be adjusted to the Consumer Price Index.

He added that the firm was considering offering investors a richer yield than the Orlando deal, which for the 2007 maturities was priced at 125 basis points over the past six month's change in the CPI.
"The level of demand from our client base picks up around 140 to 145 basis points over," he said, adding Raymond James's new the offering would be insured.
